title: Brave New World, Aldous Huxley
subject: litterature
description: In 1932, Huxley imagined a happy and stable future where freedom was given up for pleasure. Soma, genetic castes and entertainment: the other great dystopia of the 20th century.

hero.hook: What if the worst of all worlds was the one where no one wanted to be free anymore?

blocks.text: Published in **1932**, **Brave New World** by **Aldous Huxley** is the other great dystopia of the 20th century, alongside . Where Orwell imagines terror and surveillance, Huxley describes a more insidious alienation: enslavement by **pleasure**. Freedom is not taken away by force, it becomes useless, even unpleasant. **[[1984]]**

In this futuristic society, social stability and chemical happiness are worth more than individuality, deep culture or the suffering that shapes consciousness. Huxley questions a troubling paradox: can we lose our humanity in exchange for perfect comfort? His novel offers a pessimistic, but lucid, response.

sections.title: At the roots of Huxley's prophecy

blocks.text: Huxley wrote the novel as **1931**, the son of a family of British scientists and intellectuals. He observes  and **taylorism**, these methods which organize production by the assembly line and the extreme division of tasks. He transposes this industrial logic to human reproduction and conditioning. **[[Fordism and Taylorism]]**

blocks.caption: Aldous Huxley, prophet of oppression through comfort.

blocks.text: The original title, *Brave New World*, ironically quotes Shakespeare, in *The Tempest*. Naive wonder masks a dehumanized future.

Where classic dictatorships rely on fear and repression, Huxley senses a domination granted by technology, pharmacology and permanent entertainment. Her world is clean, safe, sexually liberated, and without apparent conflict. This is precisely what makes it worrying: no one feels oppressed.

sections.title: The organization of the year 632 after Ford

blocks.text: The action takes place in the year **632 after Ford**, as if the American industrialist had replaced the gods in the calendar. Five castes, from **Alphas** to **Epsilons**, are produced at conception thanks to , a technique which allows the creation of up to 96 identical twins from a single embryo. Everyone is conditioned from childhood to love their place in society. **[[Bokanovsky process]]**

blocks.caption: The assembly line: Huxley's model of human standardization.

blocks.text: Free sexuality erases exclusive attachment: “Everyone belongs to everyone. » All frustration disappears with , a comfort drug without hangovers or remorse. The family, a source of dangerous attachments and competing loyalties, has become obscene. Children are raised collectively, classic books are banned, death is trivialized from a very young age. **[[Soma]]**

sections.title: John the Savage: the clash of tragedy and comfort

blocks.text: **John the Savage**, born naturally in a **Reserve**, has read **Shakespeare** and knows suffering, shame and ecstasy. He embodies the humanist capable of authentic pain. His confrontation with **Mustapha Mond**, the World Controller who knows forbidden literature, forms the philosophical heart of the novel.
I ask for the right to be unhappy.

Mond knows what humanity has lost: literature, religion, pure science, demanding art. He sacrifices all this for public peace. John claims “the right to be unhappy”, to grow old, to fall ill, to suffer in order to understand. Refusing soma and artificial paradise, he kills himself. No reconciliation is possible between these two worldviews.

sections.title: Heritage and current affairs of the brave new world

blocks.text: More than ninety years after its publication, the novel remains strikingly relevant today. In **1958**, Huxley published , an essay in which he expressed alarm at seeing his predictions come true more quickly than he had imagined. Antidepressants, constant entertainment, commodification of the body, social networks: the list of contemporary echoes is long. **[[Return to the brave new world]]**

Orwell uses to talk about state surveillance and repression; Huxley helps analyze the slumber of democracies in comfort and immediate pleasure. His final message calls for vigilance: a humanity that no longer suffers risks no longer thinking, and a humanity that no longer thinks no longer resists.
**Brave New World** shows that we can dominate without torturing, by making freedom superfluous. Huxley reminds us that imposed happiness can be the mildest form of prison.
